question: Who was appointed as the Secretary of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Santosh Kumar Sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Santosh Kumar Sarangi** was appointed as the Secretary of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) in April 2025.

• He is a senior IAS officer from the Odisha cadre, known for his extensive administrative experience across various sectors.

• The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) plays a key role in promoting renewable energy sources like solar, wind, hydro, and biomass in India.

• Under Sarangi's leadership, the ministry aims to achieve India's ambitious renewable energy goals, including meeting its 2030 target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity.

• His appointment aligns with the government's focus on clean energy transitions, climate goals, and ensuring energy security for the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **KK Pathak**

• KK Pathak is a senior IAS officer known for his contributions to infrastructure development and urban governance reforms.

• He has held various important positions in government administration but was not appointed as the Secretary of MNRE in 2025.

• **Rajesh Kumar Sinha**

• Rajesh Kumar Sinha is a reputed civil servant recognized for his expertise in policy implementation and governance.

• He has served in multiple capacities but was not chosen for the MNRE Secretary role in April 2025.

• **Abhishek Singh**

• Abhishek Singh is an accomplished IAS officer with vast experience in digital governance and technology-led public service delivery.

• Despite his impactful work in other domains, he was not appointed as the Secretary of MNRE in 2025.

• **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**

• The MNRE is the nodal agency for all matters related to renewable energy development in India.

• India's renewable energy initiatives include flagship programs like the National Solar Mission, National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy, and Waste to Energy Programme.

• India aims to achieve 50% of its installed energy capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030 under its climate commitments.

• The ministry also collaborates with international organizations and governments to foster renewable energy research and development.
